research_topic: Is lDDT-PLI, as aggregated by PLINDER's plinder.eval, a safe single objective for an automated research agent to optimize, and what minimal aggregation change makes it non-gameable, on NVIDIA GB200 aarch64 hardware.

research_hypothesis.open_problems: plinder.eval averages per-ligand lDDT-PLI only over reference ligands that received an assignable pose, and reports PoseBusters validity as a separate column rather than gating on it. Both make the headline number gameable.
research_hypothesis.method: CG-PLI = (1/|R|) sum_i v_i s_i over ALL reference ligands, s_i := 0 when unassigned (coverage gating), v_i the PoseBusters indicator taken relative to the reference pose (validity gating). The per-ligand OpenStructure-style scorer is untouched.
research_hypothesis.experimental_setup: 150 PLINDER 2024-06/v2 MLSB test systems; controlled predictor family with utility fixed by construction; three aggregation rules compared by Spearman rank fidelity.
research_hypothesis.experimental_code:
def cg_pli(scores, valid):
    return sum(s for s, v in zip(scores, valid) if s is not None and v) / len(scores)
research_hypothesis.expected_result: PLI_ave 0.3-0.6; CG-PLI above 0.95; gap at least +0.4.
research_hypothesis.expected_conclusion: A two-line aggregation change decides whether an agent optimises structure quality or learns to abstain and emit invalid blobs.
